 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #7 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Trevon Brazile finished Thursday’s loss to the Thunder with four points (1-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs) and 12 rebounds. 
 In his official NBA debut, Brazile struggled from the field, missing all four of his three-point attempts. However, the second-round pick out of Arkansas was effective on the glass, leading the Nuggets with 12 rebounds. Brazile played 18 minutes, partly because Spencer Jones (hamstring) didn’t play. However, despite the perimeter shooting struggles, the rookie’s rebounding output was encouraging. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Spencer Jones (hamstring) is out for Saturday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 The Nuggets aren’t going to take any chances with Jones, who’s working his way back from a strained hamstring. Rookie Trevon Brazile played 18 minutes off the bench in his debut and grabbed 12 rebounds. He’s likely to take on a similar role as Aaron Gordon’s backup on Saturday. 
 Spencer Jones 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #21 
 Spencer Jones (hamstring) is out for Thursday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Jones, who strained his left hamstring early in training camp, is also navigating a right hamstring injury. His absence may give fellow reserve Trevon Brazile a few minutes, but it is unlikely to significantly affect fantasy basketball. 
 Spencer Jones 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #21 
 Spencer Jones (hamstring) is questionable for Thursday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Due to a strained left hamstring, Jones did not play at all during the preseason. He’s on the injury report for Denver’s season opener due to bilateral hamstring injury management, so his right hamstring is also a concern. If Jones can’t play, the Nuggets may have to rely on rookie Trevon Brazile a little more, with the second-round pick coming off a productive preseason. 
 Spencer Jones 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #21 
 Spencer Jones (hamstring) said on Sunday that he expects to be available for Thursday’s opener against the Thunder. 
 Jones strained his left hamstring early in training camp and did not play in any of the Nuggets’ preseason games. He’s made positive strides in his recovery, most recently doing some scrimmaging during Sunday’s practice. Following the session, Jones said that he expects to be available for Sunday’s opener. If Jones plays, there may be fewer minutes available to rookie Trevon Brazile, who played well in the Nuggets’ final preseason games. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile amassed 12 points (5-of-7 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, two assists, two steals, two blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s exhibition against the Lakers. 
 With Aaron Gordon sitting out Friday’s preseason finale, the Nuggets inserted Brazile into the starting lineup. The rookie, who dropped 22 points on Wednesday against the Clippers, had another solid outing to end his first preseason. Brazile may not play heavy minutes, but he’s clearly done enough to crack the Nuggets’ rotation right away. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile amassed 22 points (8-of-10 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Clippers. 
 The 35th overall pick in this past summer’s draft, Brazile had his most productive night of the preseason on Wednesday. The 6-foot-10 forward/center shot 80 percent from the field, and his final line lacked only an assist. Based on playing time, Brazile has already leapfrogged former first-round picks Zeke Nnaji and DaRon Holmes II in the frontcourt pecking order. He may not get the minutes needed to impact fantasy basketball once the regular season begins, but Brazile needs to be rostered in dynasty leagues. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile finished Sunday’s 109-97 loss to the Jazz with seven points, three rebounds, two blocked shots and a triple across 20 minutes. 
 The rookie out of Arkansas tied Julian Strawther for team lead in minutes, and he had a serviceable night, going 3-of-4 from the field and making an impact on defense. Denver doesn’t boast a deep bench, especially in the frontcourt, so Brazile has a real chance to earn meaningful rotation minutes in Year 1. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile notched 17 points (6-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist, three blocks and two three-pointers in Thursday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Brazile did not have his best night shooting the basketball, but the second-round pick still showed why Denver made sure to draft him. Active on the glass and defensively, the 6-foot-10 forward finished with another solid stat line. Like fellow second-round pick Bryce Hopkins, Brazile has not yet agreed to a contract, with Peyton Watson’s free agency likely a factor. However, he has the potential to contribute immediately for the Nuggets because of his athleticism and motor. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile finished Tuesday’s win over the Thunder with 32 points (11-of-19 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, one steal, one block and six three-pointers. 
 Brazile put forth his best performance of the summer on Tuesday, and he was on fire from the start. The second-round pick scored 19 points in the first half, ending it with a long three from just inside the half-court line as time expired. Brazile would score 13 more after halftime, more than holding his own against a Thunder frontcourt headlined by lottery pick Aday Mara. Because of Peyton Watson’s restricted free agency, Brazile’s contract status has not been finalized, but games like Tuesday’s likely increase his chances of landing a standard deal. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile tallied five points (2-of-8 FGs), 11 rebounds, one steal and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Rockets. 
 Brazile made his first summer league appearance on Friday, and he struggled to finish around the basket. The former Arkansas forward/center shot 2-of-7 from two, but he was active on the boards with a game-high 11 rebounds. Like fellow rookie Bryce Hopkins, Brazile has not finalized a contract as the Nuggets attend to other affairs, most notably Peyton Watson’s restricted free agency. With DaRon Holmes II a full year removed from his Achilles tear and Zeke Nnaji yet to pan out, there may be opportunities for Brazile off the bench, mainly as a defender and rebounder.

 Dejounte Murray posted a full line on Saturday with 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), six rebounds, six assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Nuggets.
 It hasn’t resulted in a win yet, but Murray has been productive to start the season. His minutes are back up after being limited last season, and he’s shooting efficiently, unlike his first year with the Pelicans. Of course, he’s still contributing value across the board, and even with Jeremiah Fears starting, he still has the ball in his hands a ton. He’ll look to keep it going in the rematch with Denver on Wednesday.

 Trey Murphy led the Pelicans with 26 points (10-of-16 FGs), six rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in a 141-135 overtime loss to the Nuggets on Saturday.
 Murphy struggled in the Pelicans’ first two games of the season, but he was able to get back on track in this one. He led New Orleans in scoring and surpassed his total points from the first two games. This type of performance was more in line with what he has been able to produce over the last two seasons, and he’ll look to keep it going in their next game, which will be a rematch with Denver on Wednesday.

 Derik Queen provided a boost off the bench with 17 points (6-of-10 FGs), eight rebounds and two assists against the Nuggets on Saturday.
 With Yves Missi (knee) sidelined for this game, head coach Jamahl Mosley opted to start DeAndre Jordan in his place. Jordan played 20 minutes, while Queen played 24 and was more productive, as expected. The Pelicans don’t play again until Wednesday, which is the first leg of a back-to-back. If Missi remains out, Queen should see a boost, and Jordan still wouldn’t be worth streaming.

 Josh Giddey accounted for nine points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Wizards.
 After shooting a combined 4-of-19 from the field in Chicago’s first two games, Giddey was considerably better on Saturday. Although he finished with just nine points, fantasy managers will be pleased with his rebounds and assists. Over three games, Giddey has shot 26.9 percent from the field and 50.0 percent from the foul line, numbers that must improve if he’s to justify his second-round ADP from the preseason.

 Norman Powell produced 18 points (4-of-12 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, four steals and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Wizards.
 Powell’s offensive role may be slightly larger than he anticipated when he signed with the Bulls, but it raises his fantasy ceiling. However, fantasy managers will reap the rewards only if he improves his accuracy. Through three games, Powell has shot 14-of-41 (34.1%) from the field, nearly 13 percentage points lower than his career number (47.0%). He’ll look to clean that up during the Bulls’ three-game Week 2, which starts on Monday in Boston.

 Matas Buzelis finished Saturday’s loss to the Wizards with 21 points (7-of-13 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Buzelis had a difficult start to the season, totaling 24 points on 4-of-17 shooting. A 13-of-16 night at the foul line in the Bulls’ season-opening loss to the Raptors gave the point total a welcome boost. He was considerably better against the Wizards, shooting over 50 percent from the field and finishing a blocked shot shy of a complete stat line. Given what he’s being asked to do as one of the Bulls’ young building blocks, Buzelis’ field-goal percentage may struggle. That said, he’s still someone who should be rostered in all fantasy leagues.

 CJ McCollum finished with 17 points (7-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer against the Rockets on Saturday.
 McCollum has been a solid scorer for Atlanta so far this season, though he hasn’t contributed much value in other categories. 14 of his 17 points in this game came in the second half, but that wasn’t enough for them to get the win. McCollum should provide more assists than he has to this point, but in category leagues, the buckets are the only thing he’ll provide consistently.

 Caleb Wilson recorded 30 points (10-of-24 FGs, 9-of-11 FTs), 14 rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Wizards.
 After an inefficient debut on Wednesday, Wilson has been excellent in the Bulls’ last two games. He finished Saturday’s defeat with his first 30-point game, making some history in the process. Wilson’s 67 points are the second-most scored by a Bulls player in their first three NBA games. The record-holder: Michael Jordan, who scored 74 points in his first three games. Wilson and the Bulls play three games in Week 2, starting with the Celtics on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Aaron Wiggins provided a boost off the bench with 16 points (6-of-13 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers against the Rockets on Saturday.
 The Man Who Saved Basketball has been fantastic for the Hawks this season. He fell out of the rotation in Oklahoma City but has been a key reserve early on for Atlanta this season. He has scored at least 15 points in every game and is averaging 17 points, 1.7 steals and 3.3 three-pointers per game while shooting 58.1 percent from the floor. As a backup, Wiggins may not be able to keep up this pace, but he should hold streaming appeal if he gets a spot start from time to time. For now, he’ll just continue to be a high-level backup.

 After putting up 34 points in his first appearance in a Wizards uniform on Wednesday, Davis crashed back to earth against the Raptors on Friday. The good news for fantasy managers was that the veteran forward/center performed better in Chicago, even with the subpar percentages. Davis and the Wizards play two of their three Week 2 games against the Hornets, which should be good matchups for him. In between those games is one against the Cavaliers.
